Choose a commutative diagram
<MATH_0001>
where <MATH_0002> and <MATH_0003> are algebraic spaces, the vertical arrows are smooth,
and <MATH_0004> surjective. There is a maximal open subspace
<MATH_0005> such that <MATH_0006> is smooth, see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0007> be the open substack
corresponding to the image of <MATH_0008>
(Properties of Stacks, Lemmas <REF_0002> and
<REF_0003>).
By the equivalence in Lemma <REF_0004>
we find that <MATH_0009> is smooth
and that <MATH_0010> is the largest open substack with this
property.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assertion (1) follows from the fact that being smooth
is smooth local on the source (this property was used to even define
smooth morphisms of algebraic stacks).
Assertions (2) and (3) follow from the case of algebraic spaces, see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0005>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces.
Let <MATH_0002> be a group algebraic space over <MATH_0003> which is flat
and locally of finite presentation over <MATH_0004>. Let <MATH_0005> act on <MATH_0006> over <MATH_0007>.
Then the quotient stack <MATH_0008> is smooth over <MATH_0009>.

<STRUCT_0001>
This holds even if <MATH_0001> is not smooth over <MATH_0002>!

The quotient <MATH_0001> is an algebraic stack by
Criteria for Representability, Theorem
<REF_0001>.
The smoothness of <MATH_0002> over <MATH_0003> follows from the fact that smoothness
descends under fppf coverings:
Choose a surjective smooth morphism <MATH_0004> where <MATH_0005> is a scheme.
Smoothness of <MATH_0006> over <MATH_0007> is equivalent to smoothness of <MATH_0008> over <MATH_0009>.
Observe that <MATH_0010> is smooth over <MATH_0011> and hence smooth
over <MATH_0012> (because compositions of smooth morphisms are smooth).
On the other hand, <MATH_0013> is locally of
finite presentation, flat, and surjective (because it is
the base change of <MATH_0014> which has those properties
for example by Criteria for Representability, Lemma
<REF_0002>).
Therefore we may apply Descent on Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0003>.
